## E. Glossary of Technical Terms

**BTO / BaTiO₃ (Barium Titanate):** Ferroelectric oxide with a large Pockels electro-optic coefficient; deposited by ROSIE on silicon substrates to fabricate high-speed optical modulators.

**EAR (Export Administration Regulations):** US Commerce Department rules governing the export of dual-use goods and technologies, including semiconductor manufacturing equipment, to restricted end-users or destinations.

**FOUP (Front-Opening Unified Pod):** Standardised wafer-carrier cassette used in 300 mm CMOS fabs; ROSIE's cassette automation is FOUP-compatible for integration into existing fab workflows.

**HEMT (High-Electron-Mobility Transistor):** III-V device architecture (GaAs, InP, GaN) requiring precisely doped heterostructure epiwafers grown by MBE; used in 5G/6G RF front ends.

**MBE (Molecular Beam Epitaxy):** Physical vapour deposition under ultra-high vacuum (below 10⁻¹⁰ torr) producing atomically precise single-crystal semiconductor thin films; Riber's core product domain.

**NQCP (Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme):** Danish quantum-computing initiative hosted at the Niels Bohr Institute; first ROSIE customer via the POEM pilot line.

**POEM (Photonic Oxide Epitaxy Modulator Technology):** Riber's joint pilot-line initiative with NQCP to demonstrate BTO-on-silicon electro-optic modulator fabrication using the ROSIE platform.

**ROSIE (RIBER Oxide on Silicon Epitaxy):** Riber's 300 mm silicon-compatible, SEMI-standard MBE platform for depositing BTO and STO films; commercially launched in 2025.

**SEMI:** Global semiconductor equipment and materials industry association; its standards (e.g., SEMI E standards for equipment interfaces, FOUP specifications) define fab-automation interoperability requirements that ROSIE is engineered to satisfy.

**STO (Strontium Titanate / SrTiO₃):** Oxide buffer layer deposited alongside BTO in silicon-photonics epitaxy stacks to manage lattice mismatch and interface quality.

**UHV (Ultra-High Vacuum):** Operating pressure regime below 10⁻⁷ Pa (approximately 10⁻⁹ torr) required for MBE deposition; Riber's founding expertise in UHV hardware underpins all product lines.

**VCSEL (Vertical-Cavity Surface-Emitting Laser):** Compact semiconductor laser emitting perpendicular to the wafer surface; fabricated from MBE-grown GaAs or InP heterostructures for 3D sensing, LiDAR, and datacom applications.

financials.key_finding:
Riber SA is a micro-to-small-cap French industrial equipment company with annual revenues of €40–41 million and a market capitalisation in the approximate range of €115–320 million as of mid-2026 (figures vary materially across data sources given thin trading liquidity on Euronext Growth Paris; shares outstanding approximately 21.25 million). The company has demonstrated a clear and accelerating profitability inflection over the 2023–2025 fiscal cycle: revenues grew from €27.8 million in fiscal 2022 to €39.2 million in 2023 (+41%, driven almost entirely by a near-doubling in MBE systems deliveries), to €41.2 million in 2024 (+4.9%), before a modest decline to €40.3 million in 2025 (−2.1%). Against this essentially flat top-line trajectory since 2023, net income has compounded sharply: from €3.4 million in 2023 (8.7% margin) to €4.1 million in 2024 (10.0% margin) to €5.2 million in 2025 (13.0% margin), a 53% cumulative increase in net income on a 3% cumulative revenue increase. Gross margin expanded from approximately 34% in 2023 to 36.1% in 2024 and 38.6% in 2025, reflecting mix shift toward production systems (higher ASPs, improved overhead absorption) and pricing discipline in the accessories segment. Operating income reached €5.1 million in 2025 (12.7% of revenue), up 13.5% year-on-year.

The balance sheet is modestly capitalised and conservatively structured: shareholders' equity was €27.3 million at year-end 2025, up €3.7 million from 2024, reflecting accumulated net income; cash and cash equivalents were €7.5 million at December 31, 2025 (down from €8.6 million at end-2024), with the reduction attributable to working-capital investment supporting H2 deliveries and the proposed dividend payment. Riber carries no significant financial debt, making the capital structure essentially equity-funded with minimal leverage. The Board proposed a €0.10 per share dividend for 2025 (payable June 2026), a 25% increase over the prior-year payout, consistent with a progressive dividend policy tied to earnings growth.

Revenue lumpiness is a structural feature: H1 2025 revenues were €10.7 million (−22% year-on-year) while H2 2025 revenues were €29.5 million (+7%), a 73%/27% back-half concentration that reflects the long lead times and customer-acceptance milestones embedded in MBE system delivery schedules. The order book entering 2026 at €26.9 million (+24%) provides meaningful forward visibility but does not fully eliminate half-year revenue variability.
structural_observations: Revenue base of €40–41m annually since 2023 is dominated by MBE systems (~77% of revenue in 2025, €30.9m), with services and accessories providing a recurring buffer (~23%, €9.4m); the 2025 services decline of 7.8% was attributed partly to US government budgetary constraints reducing university laboratory procurement.

Fiscal year cadence is heavily H2-weighted: H1 2025 represented only 26.6% of full-year revenue (€10.7m), while H2 2025 delivered 73.4% (€29.5m); this pattern is structurally driven by machine acceptance schedules and customer factory readiness, creating significant interim P&L volatility that does not reflect underlying business health.

Margin progression is the defining financial narrative of the Geoffroy era: gross margin has expanded approximately 450 basis points from FY 2023 to FY 2025, operating margin reached 12.7% in 2025, and net margin reached 13.0%—the highest in the company's recent history—suggesting structural rather than cyclical improvement in cost absorption and pricing.

Capital structure is debt-free with shareholders' equity of €27.3m and cash of €7.5m at year-end 2025; the absence of financial leverage means earnings are not amplified by interest coverage but also that the balance sheet is resilient in downturns; Riber funds R&D internally and has not required external equity financing in the recent reporting period.

Geographic revenue concentration is a two-edged structural variable: Asia (primarily Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, China) constituted 57.3% of 2024 revenue before falling to 39.7% in 2025 as European and North American deliveries accelerated; export-licence risk is embedded in the Asian segment given semiconductor equipment trade controls, and €4 million of 2025 opportunities were blocked by refusals.

Comparable peers in MBE equipment include Veeco Instruments (Nasdaq: VECO), a US-listed compound-semiconductor and silicon-technology equipment company with revenues of approximately $600m and far broader product scope; DCA Instruments (Finland, private) and SVT Associates (US, private) operate in research-grade MBE but are not publicly comparable; Riber's pure-play MBE focus, European listing, and sub-€50m revenue scale make it a difficult peer-group match for institutional equity analysis.

Market capitalisation has been highly volatile: shares outstanding are approximately 21.25 million on Euronext Growth Paris (thin float, minimal sell-side coverage); reported 365-day price appreciation of approximately +384% through May 2026 suggests the stock re-rated sharply—likely on ROSIE commercial traction and profitability improvement—and the resulting market cap in the €300m range implies a price-to-earnings multiple well above historical norms that will require sustained ROSIE revenue conversion to justify.

leadership.key_finding:
Riber SA's leadership structure is defined by the singular figure of Annie Geoffroy, whose appointment as Chairwoman and CEO in June 2024 completed a two-step consolidation of authority that began when she transitioned from Supervisory Board President to Management Board President in September 2023. Geoffroy, approximately 70 years old, holds an ESCP Europe degree and a DESS in Management Control, and built her career in the general management of French industrial companies with an emphasis on financial oversight and operational transformation; she has operated as a transition manager since 2015. Her dual-hat role as Chair and CEO is permissible under the MiddleNext Governance Code for smaller listed companies and concentrates strategic and operational decision-making more tightly than Riber's prior bifurcated structure allowed.

The seven-member Board of Directors established at the June 2024 general meeting comprises: Geoffroy (Chair/CEO), Sylviane Troadec (independent), Nicolas Grandjean (independent, academic profile consistent with a compound-semiconductor researcher), Didier Cornardeau (independent), Alexandre Jevakhoff (independent), Pierre-Yves Kielwasser, and Bernard Raboutet. Five of the seven directors are identified as independent; the board's term runs through the 2027 AGM deliberating on FY 2026 accounts. No private equity sponsor or controlling family shareholder has been identified in the public record, suggesting diffuse institutional and retail ownership typical of Euronext Growth small-caps.

The prior Management Board included Michel Picault and Emmanuel Routier alongside Geoffroy. No detailed CFO biography is publicly available; Riber's investor relations materials do not identify a dedicated Chief Financial Officer separate from the CEO structure. Financial accounts are audited by KPMG and RSM Paris. The governance code adhered to is the MiddleNext Corporate Governance Code for mid-caps and small-caps listed in France.
research_notes_for_writer: Verify whether Michel Picault and Emmanuel Routier retained roles after the June 2024 governance restructuring; their titles under the prior Management Board structure (members alongside Geoffroy) suggest operational or divisional responsibilities that may persist under the new unitary board—identify whether either holds a CFO, COO, or equivalent executive title.

Seek out the full transcript or extended summary of Annie Geoffroy's interview with La Bourse et la Vie TV ('nous avons vocation à élargir notre marché') for strategic framing verbatim quotes; this appears to be the most substantive long-form CEO interview in the public record and likely covers ROSIE, export controls, and market expansion philosophy.

Nicolas Grandjean on the Riber board warrants specific investigation: a French academic named Nicolas Grandjean is a prominent III-V nitride semiconductor researcher at EPFL (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne); if this is the same person, his presence as an independent director signals the board's technical depth and may reveal informal research collaborations or academic customer relationships.

Determine shareholder structure more precisely: Euronext Growth listings often have a founding family or management bloc holding 20–40% of shares; identify the top five shareholders via AMF (Autorité des marchés financiers) public declaration records and French company registry (INPI), as concentrated ownership affects capital allocation decisions and takeout optionality.

Quantify the separation between Chair and CEO roles under MiddleNext Code compliance: the code recommends dissociation of powers for companies above certain size thresholds; for a company of Riber's scale the combined Chair/CEO is compliant but warrants a section on independence risk and succession planning, especially given Geoffroy's approximate age of 70.

Examine board committee structure: the governance page does not list formal audit, remuneration, or nominations committees; determine whether such committees exist informally or by charter under the updated internal board regulations (posted June 2024) and whether KPMG's audit engagement has raised any independence or reporting concerns in recent statutory accounts.

Investigate Annie Geoffroy's transition-management mandate context: her prior role as Supervisory Board President, followed by the move to Management Board in September 2023, may reflect a specific corporate event—possible CEO departure, performance crisis, or strategic pivot—that triggered the governance change pre-dating the formal June 2024 restructuring; understanding this transition backstory is material to the leadership chapter narrative.
